Test that the enumerator gets and enforces its declared timeout (#280)

This message compares the tree it merges with main as of #275 (Refresh
the vendored AIQT hooks plugin), the commit of main that the branch
merged first, not one commit of the branch with another. The branch
later merged 2 later commits of main, so the tree also holds main's
own changes from main as of #275 (Refresh the vendored AIQT hooks
plugin) to the later of them; each comparison below leaves those
changes out, and this message does not list them, apart from how the
last merge resolves tools/test-orch-stage2-hooks.py. The branch
started from main as of #271 (State the full download's character
count as saved); against main as of #271 (State the full download's
character count as saved) the tree also differs by main's own changes
from main as of #271 (State the full download's character count as
saved) to main as of #275 (Refresh the vendored AIQT hooks plugin), in
26 more files, the hook among them.

In main as of #275 (Refresh the vendored AIQT hooks plugin),
T15EnumeratorTimeout in tools/test-orch-stage2-hooks.py
holds 2 tests. test_sleeping_enumerator_times_out_and_denies declares
an enumerator that sleeps 30 s under a declared timeout of 1 s, runs
the hook through run_hook with a 120 s limit on the call, and requires
exit 2, ENUMERATOR_ERROR and 'failed to run' in stderr, and that the
whole Stop hook call ended within 15 s. test_stage1_contrast requires,
for the stage 1 registry, which declares no enumerator, the hook's
NO_ENUMERATOR deny, exit 2 with NO_ENUMERATOR in stderr, and no
'failed to run'. So a host slow enough to stretch the call to 15 s
failed the correct hook, and no test checked whether the enumerator
was still running when the hook returned or which timeout value the
hook passed.

The 15 s bound is gone. Both enumerator tests and the 2 stage 1 tests
run the unchanged hook through REAPER_PROG, a python3 -I wrapper that
is the Linux child subreaper, so every process that the hook starts
stays its descendant. It waits up to 120 s for the hook to exit and
kills it if it has not, notes whether a process that the hook started
is still alive, then sends SIGKILL to each of its children, reaps them
and repeats until it has no child left or the 30 s cleanup bound,
which it checks before each pass, has passed, and writes a JSON
report. It signals only its own unreaped children, so no signal can
reach an unrelated process.

What can outlive a test: every process under the wrapper when the
wrapper ends before its cleanup has finished, which happens when the
test's limit on the wrapper call kills it, when another signal ends
it, such as one that the hook sends it, or when an error ends it; the
wrapper's children still alive when cleanup stops at the 30 s bound,
which the report lists, and their descendants; and a process that the
hook gets another program, such as a service manager, to start.
Cleanup stops at its bound with a child alive when a process survives
SIGKILL that long, such as one in uninterruptible sleep, or when the
wrapper itself does not run for that long, such as when it is stopped
or kept off the CPU, and then it may have sent no SIGKILL. In each
case but the last the test fails. The test's limit on the wrapper
call is 240 s for the 4 tests that run the hook, 90 s past the
wrapper's bounds of 120 s and 30 s, and 60 s for the 2 wrapper tests,
20 s past their bounds of 10 s and 30 s; in a wrapper test the
processes under the wrapper include the stand-in hook's child and
grandchild, which sleep 90 s. Without the prctl call or
/proc/self/task/*/children the wrapper exits with a message and the
tests fail.

test_wrapper_kills_processes_in_another_session and
test_wrapper_kills_a_hook_that_does_not_exit run a stand-in hook that
takes a shared lock and starts a child in another session, which
starts a grandchild; the stand-in exits at once, or sleeps past a 10 s
hook bound. Once the wrapper returns, each requires that it can take
the lock exclusively, so none of the 3 processes is alive.

The 4 tests that run the hook run the hook file in a process whose
subprocess.run is replaced by RECORDING_HOOK_PROG, a recorder that
logs the argv and timeout argument of each call. In strip mode it
makes each real call without the timeout. In keep mode it makes the
real call unchanged for the declared enumerator argv only, and also
logs its outcome, 'returned' or the type name of the exception that
it raised, which it raises again; it makes every other call without
the timeout. In the enforcement test the hook's only other call is git
rev-parse --show-toplevel in _recovery_toplevel, with a 5 s timeout;
if that timeout fired, as it can on a loaded host, _orch_stop_family
would allow the stop without running the enumerator, and the test
would fail. In both modes the recorder also adds an audit hook that
logs, to a second file, each audit event that starts a process
(subprocess.Popen, os.system, os.exec, os.posix_spawn, os.spawn,
os.fork and _posixsubprocess.fork_exec), with the argv of each
subprocess.Popen event. A process that native code starts without an
audit event is not logged. FIRST_FORK_FAILS_PROG is the recorder with
a start that makes the first os.fork call of the hook's process raise
the os.fork audit event and then BlockingIOError, as CPython's os.fork
does when fork() fails; every later call forks.

test_sleeping_enumerator_times_out_and_denies declares an enumerator,
SLEEPING_ENUM_FIXTURE, that is 1 process that records its start when
its environment names a file for that and then sleeps 100 s, under a
declared timeout of 1 s, and runs the hook in keep mode. The test asks
the enumerator to do nothing but that record before the timeout fires,
and it sleeps 100 s, so a call that passes it a 1 s timeout raises
TimeoutExpired once that timeout fires, unless the enumerator cannot
be started or the 120 s bound kills the hook first. The test
requires, in this order, that the wrapper call ended within 240 s and
the wrapper wrote its report, that no process that the hook started
was alive when cleanup stopped, at once or after 30 s, and that the
hook exited within 120 s; then exactly 1 call with the declared argv,
timeout 1 and outcome TimeoutExpired; then no process that the hook
started still running when it ended; then exit 2, ENUMERATOR_ERROR
and 'failed to run'. Its time bounds are the 240 s, 30 s and 120 s
ones; every other check is logical, and no timeout of the hook but the
enumerator's can fire. A correct hook leaves no process running, so
cleanup has nothing to do, and for such a hook only the 240 s and
120 s bounds can make a check's result depend on load.

test_declared_timeout_reaches_the_enumerator_call runs the hook in
strip mode for each declared timeout of 0.001, 1, 7.5 and 60 s and
requires the same 3 time bounds and report, then exactly 1 call with
the declared argv and that timeout argument, and that the enumerator
ran once.

test_stage1_contrast runs the hook in strip mode for the stage 1
registry and requires the same 3 time bounds and report, then no
process left running, then that the hook's only subprocess.run call
was the git call in _recovery_toplevel, then that the process starts
logged were that call's and the children that the hook's main() forks
to check that it can read a child's exit status, and no other, then
exit 2, NO_ENUMERATOR and no 'failed to run'. The children are 1 when
the first probe reads its child's status; when it refuses, main() of
the fail-open stop guard restores SIGCHLD to SIG_DFL, probes again and
notes the restore on stderr, and probe_forks then expects 1 more os.fork
event unless the first probe refused before it called os.fork. So the
hook started no other process by subprocess, os.system, os.exec*,
os.posix_spawn, os.spawn* or os.fork, and left none running.
test_stage1_contrast_after_the_first_probe_fork_fails makes the same
checks through FIRST_FORK_FAILS_PROG, where the start check expects 2
os.fork events, and requires the restore note after the reason that
the probe could not fork. In main as of #275 (Refresh the vendored
AIQT hooks plugin) test_stage1_contrast runs the hook through
run_hook, without the recorder or the wrapper, and fails a correct
hook when that call's 5 s timeout fires.
test_stage1_contrast_when_sigchld_is_ignored runs test_stage1_contrast
in a nested python3 -I process of the file that SIGCHLD_IGNORED_PROG
starts with SIGCHLD ignored, within a 300 s bound, 60 s past the
nested wrapper call's 240 s, and requires that it ran 1 test and
exited 0. A process that ignores SIGCHLD reads the exit status of each
process that it starts as 0 and passes the disposition on across
exec, so with the process that starts the file ignoring SIGCHLD the
test before this change read the hook's exit 2 deny as exit 0, as did
other tests of the file. The file now sets SIGCHLD to SIG_DFL when it
loads, before it starts any process. The test misses a start with
SIGCHLD at SIG_DFL and SA_NOCLDWAIT set, which it does not arrange.

Outside the T15EnumeratorTimeout section the test file differs from
main as of #275 (Refresh the vendored AIQT hooks plugin) only by the
import of signal, the setting of SIGCHLD to SIG_DFL with its comment,
the TEST_TIME_LIMITS table, the comment above it and the check of
time limits after it, which wraps assertLess, assertLessEqual and run
of unittest.TestCase and threading.Thread.join when the file loads,
1 call of that check in run_doctor_recorded with 1 sentence of its
docstring, the comment above Stage2Harness, the Stage2TimeLimitProbe,
TimeLimitSinkProbe and TimeLimitTeardownProbe classes with the
function and the program that they use, the HookRangeProbe class
with PART_RANGES and
hook_statement_lines, the 3 statements that read the sites of time
limits before the audit hook is added, with their comment, the stage
1 line range that the
comment of assert_no_enumerator_deny cites, and hook line citations,
with the words beside 3 of them, in comments, in the module docstring
and in strings of PRECHECK_SITES, corrected to start and end on the
statements that the words beside them name; the code of run_hook and
of every other test, and the hook, are as in main as of #275 (Refresh
the vendored AIQT hooks plugin), and each test runs with those
wrappers and that call. A review of each range that the file cites,
against the statements of the hook and the words beside it, found
those ranges, the section header's 22831-22835 among them, which now
ends on 22836. HookRangeProbe requires each range that the file or
tools/test-orch-stage1-hooks.py cites to start on the first line of a
statement or except clause of the hook and end on the last line of
one, apart from 10 that cite part of a statement on purpose; it does
not check that a range names what the words beside it name. Every
other test that runs the hook, or the doctor, keeps the hook's own
timeouts: the 5 s one of the git call in _recovery_toplevel, the 5 s
or 10 s one of any other git call, the declared enumerator timeout,
ENUM_TIMEOUT, 60 s, in the stage 2 fixture, and for orch_yield_tool and
orch_ask_guard the 8 s PreToolUse deadline.
Such a test fails a correct hook when one of them fires and that
changes what the test checks, and passes when it requires only what
the hook also does after that timeout, as T04NotBefore's
test_future_blocks requires only exit 0. These tests also set limits
of their own, which TEST_TIME_LIMITS lists by the class and function
of the site that applies each, 21 entries with the least value that
each site applies. The least is 4.5 s, at
DoctorScopeMargin._assert_refused_near, which puts NEAR on the time
from just before a case sets its lease mtime 4.5 s from a freshness
bound of the hook to the return of the doctor call; the others are
60 s, 119 s, 120 s, 240 s and 300 s, and 60 s or 240 s through
run_reaped.
So, deriving from the 2 lists, a correct hook can fail such a test
when the doctor call of a DoctorScopeMargin case takes 4.5 s, while
its git call is still inside its 5 s timeout, and otherwise only when
1 git call takes 5 s, or 10 s for a 10 s call, a declared enumerator
takes its declared timeout, a PreToolUse action takes 8 s, or 1 call
reaches its limit, which is at least the value that TEST_TIME_LIMITS
gives its site. A fixture time that a slow host could carry across a
bound of the hook is not counted, apart from DoctorScopeMargin's. The
comment above Stage2Harness gives both lists, with the hook line of
each hook timeout, the reason the tests
keep the hook's timeouts, which is that they check the installed hook
as the platform runs it, and this bound.

Each limit is checked when it is applied, whatever way its value was
bound. A limit is applied at 1 of 3 sinks: a launch through
run_doctor_recorded, through which the file's audit hook forces
every launch of the test process; the bound b of an assertLess or
assertLessEqual call, which every such call in the process is taken
to be; and the timeout of threading.Thread.join. The file wraps the 2
asserts and Thread.join, each with its own parameters, and
run_doctor_recorded gives its timeout to the check before the run
starts. The site of a limit is the innermost frame that runs a
function at the top level of the file or a method defined in a class
of the file, keyed by class and function and told by the identity of
its code, which the file maps from each function's __qualname__ once
it is defined; code nested in such a function has its site. The
sinks and the wrapper of unittest.TestCase.run have none, so a limit
applied where no other frame runs the file's code, such as by a
cleanup that is a sink or by a test of another module, has no site
and is checked against the floor only. The check
uses neither co_qualname nor the f_locals proxy, as the CI job runs
the python3 of ubuntu-latest, whose version the workflow does not
pin. Before the sink runs it refuses a value that is not an int or a
float; anywhere in the process, a value below 4.5 s, the least value
of the table, also where no frame has a site; and, at a site of a
Stage2Harness test, a site that the table does not list or a value
below the value that it gives the site. It compares by not value >=
floor, so it refuses NaN. Each test in the process gets a cleanup that
fails it for each refusal recorded while it ran, also one raised in
a thread or caught by the test. tearDownModule fails the run for a
refusal that no cleanup read, of those raised before it reads them,
and, once every test of the file, as a new unittest.TestLoader finds
them, has run in the process, so not in a run that a -k option
narrows, for each entry whose site admitted no limit or whose value
is not the least value admitted at its site. A refusal raised after
that, while no test runs, such as in a thread still running once
tearDownModule has run, is read by nothing: in a thread it stops only
that thread, and the run's result and exit status are as they would
be without it.
Not checked: a limit that reaches none of the 3 sinks, such as an
elapsed time compared in an if statement or the timeout of
signal.alarm, code that bypasses the wrappers, apart from launches, a
limit on a path that no run takes, and a limit inside a program
string of the file. Stage2TimeLimitProbe requires each entry to be a
site of a Stage2Harness test, and the comment above Stage2Harness,
with V the least value, to hold "least of them is" exactly once, as
"The least of them is V s, at L.", where L names the sites of exactly
the entries that hold V, each once, in any order, and to follow each
"least of them is" and "least test limit is" in it with " V s". It
plants 13 comments and tables that must each give a mismatch, such as
a comment that names another site as the holder of the least value
and names the holder in another sentence, one that states a second
least value, and one that states the least value again in a line
that it comments out, and 5 controls that must give none. It also
requires time_limit_full_run, which tells tearDownModule whether
every test has run, to take the 1 test that a name pattern on
unittest.defaultTestLoader selects, as a -k option gives it, as no
full run and every test of the file as one, with and without that
pattern. TimeLimitSinkProbe runs 29 planted cases in
the process: 17 forms that bind a limit of 1 s without a plain call,
such as super(), an alias, getattr, functools.partial, type(self), an
override's default, a match class pattern, inspect.getmembers,
operator.methodcaller and gc.get_objects, and 9 more refusals, each of
which must fail its case before its sink applies the limit, and 3
controls at 60 s through run_reaped and at 4.5 s, each of which must
pass with its limit admitted. In a planted case run in a thread of
its own, whose cleanup calls a sink directly, 60 s at Thread.join and
at assertLess must be admitted at no site, and 4.4 s at Thread.join
refused at the floor. TimeLimitTeardownProbe holds 1 test, which
requires that it is the last test of the file that a
unittest.TestLoader finds. It calls tearDownModule with TESTS_RUN,
TIME_LIMIT_CHECKS and TIME_LIMIT_REFUSALS replaced for the call and
TIME_LIMIT_LOCK, which is reentrant, held until it restores them, so
a limit that a thread applies meanwhile waits for the lock and is
recorded in the restored lists: with every test of the file run, it
must fail with the mismatch of an entry whose site admitted a greater
least limit and of one whose site admitted none; with 1 test missing,
or with that test alone, it must fail for neither; and limits that
agree with the table must fail neither run. Once every test of the
file has run, as in a full run, the test requires each entry to be
the least limit admitted at its site, so a wrong entry fails the test
itself, not only tearDownModule; a run that -k narrows does not reach
that check. The T15EnumeratorTimeout section header states that the
hook exits within 120 s, not that it never hangs, so in
tools/test-no-qa-labels.py only 2 allowlist entries, which hold the
exact text of that line and of the comment that cites the
NO_ENUMERATOR check and its return and the stage 1 test of that deny,
differ from main as of #275 (Refresh the vendored AIQT hooks plugin).
In tools/test-orch-stage1-hooks.py only 1 entry of the WHOLE table of
WholeFunctionCitations, 4 hook line ranges in comments and 1 sentence
of the docstring of WholeFunctionCitations differ from main as
of #275 (Refresh the vendored AIQT hooks plugin): the comment of
test_stage1_contrast cites the whole of _child_status_refusal by its
line range in the hook, and that test requires each whole-function
citation in a tools file to be counted in WHOLE; the 4 ranges now
start and end on the statements that they name, and the sentence
states that the count takes any first line from the def line to the
first line of the body after any docstring. The branch also adds
.github/squash/280.txt, which holds this message and which the pull
request text check reads.

The enforcement test fails a hook that passes no timeout argument, as
it waits the 100 s sleep out, on the call check if the hook still
exits within 120 s and on the "exited" check, which comes first, if it
does not; a hook that passes a timeout argument other than 1, on the
call check if the hook still exits within 120 s, as with a fixed 20 s,
60 s or 180 s, max(timeout, 30) or timeout * 2, and on the "exited"
check if it does not; a hook that runs the enumerator again after a
timeout, which records 2 or more calls, on the call check if the hook
still exits within 120 s and on the "exited" check if it does not; a
hook that starts the enumerator with Popen, waits the declared timeout
and never stops it, in or out of a new session, as it records no call
(it also leaves the enumerator running, but the test stops at the call
check, before its check for a process left running); a hook that takes
the timeout as success or gives another verdict; a hook that stalls
long enough not to exit within 120 s; and a change to the hook's check
of the declared value that rejects 1, as the hook then passes its 60 s
fallback.

The recorder test fails a hook that passes the same timeout whatever
is declared, such as 1 s, 20 s or 60 s, for at least 3 of the 4
values, and fails timeout * 2 and no timeout argument for all 4. The
value 0.001 fails a floor above it, such as max(timeout, 1) or
max(timeout, 30); 60 fails a cap below it, such as min(timeout, 30);
and 7.5 fails rounding to a whole number. It also fails a change to
the hook's check of the declared value that rejects 0.001, 1 or 7.5,
such as one that accepts only an int, for that value, as the hook then
passes its 60 s fallback. It does not catch a change that rejects 60,
as the hook then passes its 60 s fallback for the declared 60, the
same value.

The enforcement test passes a hook that passes 1 s whatever is
declared, or that changes only values other than 1, such as
round(timeout); the recorder test fails each such change to 0.001, 7.5
or 60.

Hook variants that neither enumerator test catches:
- a stall after the timeout, or before the hook starts the enumerator,
  that still lets the hook exit within 120 s, such as a 5 s sleep in
  the except handler or before the enumerator starts. The 15 s bound
  on the whole call in main as of #275 (Refresh the vendored AIQT hooks
  plugin) caught such a stall only when the whole call then passed
  15 s, which a 5 s stall after the 1 s timeout need not bring about,
  and it also failed the correct hook once a loaded host stretched the
  call past 15 s;
- a floor of 0.001 or below, such as max(timeout, 0.001);
- a cap of a declared timeout between 60 s and 600 s, such as
  min(timeout, 60) or min(timeout, 300), which the declared-timeout
  test no longer catches, as it declares at most ENUM_TIMEOUT, 60 s,
  since write_registry refuses a declared timeout over it;
- a cap of 600 or above, such as min(timeout, 600), which changes
  nothing, as the hook's check already rejects a value above 600;
- rounding to 3 or more decimal places, such as round(timeout, 3);
- a change to a declared value other than 0.001, 1, 7.5 and 60, such
  as 60 s for any value from 10 to 599;
- a change to the 60 s fallback, such as 30 s, and a change to which
  values the check rejects (not a number, 0 or below, or above 600)
  that still accepts 0.001, 1, 7.5 and 60, such as one that rejects
  JSON true, which the unchanged hook takes as a timeout of 1 s, or one
  that rejects each value over 60;
- a change to the check that rejects 60 and still accepts 0.001, 1 and
  7.5, such as 0 < timeout < 60, as the hook then passes its 60 s
  fallback for the declared 60, the same value;
- a hook that stops only the enumerator's own process, as the
  unchanged hook's timeout does, against one that also stops the
  processes that the enumerator starts: the sleeping enumerator is 1
  process, so the tests say nothing about processes that an enumerator
  starts.

Other limits:
- The tests do not time the effective timeout. Enforcement rests on
  subprocess.run honouring its timeout argument, and is seen once, as
  TimeoutExpired, in a run where the enumerator sleeps 100 s.
- A hook that starts the enumerator other than through subprocess.run
  records no call and fails both enumerator tests, even if it enforces
  the declared value.
- The stage 1 tests pass a hook whose extra process native code starts
  without an audit event, unless that process is still running when
  the hook ends, and a hook that gets another program, such as a
  service manager, to start a process. Their start check takes the
  hook's restore note as the account of what its first probe met, so
  it passes a hook that writes that note and forks as the note states.

The enforcement test counts no heartbeat. A heartbeat design runs an
enumerator that writes 1 line a second, requires fewer than 5 lines,
and requires that the hook spent less than 0.5 s after the enumerator
ended, read from the hook's /proc/<pid>/schedstat. To take that
reading, it requires the enumerator to write the hook's process id to
a FIFO before the declared 1 s runs out. A review run of that design
reported that a correct hook failed that requirement on 1 CPU shared
with 48 busy loops, and that a copy that passes round(timeout), the
same 1 s for this test, failed the 0.5 s bound under heavy load. This
message does not rest on a reproduction of either report; it rests on
the design, in which a correct hook passes only if the enumerator wins
a race against the hook's 1 s deadline and the hook keeps within a
small time margin.

The enforcement test asks the enumerator to do nothing but record its
start, which no check of that test reads, before the timeout fires,
and the enumerator sleeps 100 s, so no check needs the enumerator to
do work within the 1 s, and apart from its 3 time bounds the test
asserts only outcomes. For a hook that calls subprocess.run, the line
count fails a hook that keeps the enumerator alive long enough to
write 5 lines, about 4 s, such as one that passes a timeout of that
length or more, or none; the enforcement test fails every timeout
argument other than 1, and no timeout argument. The maintainer chose
a heartbeat test for the kill plus a test that the hook passes exactly
the declared timeout; the tree keeps both roles, a kill test and an
exact value test, and has no heartbeat count.

This message supersedes the messages of the branch's commits: it is the
message that lands on main, and it states what the branch changes. It
does not check those messages against their diffs, and it does not list
or correct their statements. Some of those statements are not borne out
by their diffs, and later messages of the branch correct some of them,
so a reader should take a statement of one of those messages as borne
out only where this message makes it too. Below, the branch's 29 commits
up to and including the one that carries this message are numbered from
1, its first, to 29, that one, with the merge commit that merges main as
of #275 (Refresh the vendored AIQT hooks plugin) as 9, and the merge
commits that merge the 2 later commits of main as 24 and 25. Commit 21,
"Rerun the required checks on an unchanged tree", changes no file, and
commit 23, "Name the real subject of the last revision and refill the
squash text", is a text fix. Commit 26, "Describe the second join of
main and its coverage gap", is a text fix; commit 27, "Count the text
commits and correct the 60 s claim", corrects this message, the
description of the pull request and the comments of the 2 enumerator
tests in tools/test-orch-stage2-hooks.py; commit 28, "Correct the text
commit subjects and match the residual lists", corrects this message,
the description of the pull request and the comment of the
T15EnumeratorTimeout section of that file; and commit 29, "Align the 2
texts on each fact", corrects this message, the description of the
pull request and the comment of the T15EnumeratorTimeout section of
that file. Up to commit 29, no other commit is on the branch.

Commit 25 resolves 3 conflict blocks in
tools/test-orch-stage2-hooks.py, where main's changes refuse a
declared enumerator whose program is not 1 of ENUM_PROGRAMS, and a
declared timeout over ENUM_TIMEOUT, 60 s, and widen the bounds of the
doctor and hook calls that can run the stage 2 enumerator to
RUN_TIMEOUT, 120 s. In the head of
test_sleeping_enumerator_times_out_and_denies it keeps this branch's
test, with main's SLEEPING_ENUM_FIXTURE as the enumerator, and drops
main's comment on its 90 s bound; at the end of that test and in
test_declared_timeout_reaches_the_enumerator_call it keeps this
branch's test and drops main's 90 s bound on the elapsed time, which
the wider 120 s hook bound replaces; and in run_doctor_recorded it
joins both docstrings and checks the limit before main's code makes
the run's file of enumerator starts. The sleeping enumerator is now
the pinned SLEEPING_ENUM_FIXTURE, which sleeps 100 s in place of
3600 s, so a hook that waits the sleep out fails the call check if it
still exits within 120 s, and the earlier "exited" check if not. The
declared timeouts are capped at ENUM_TIMEOUT,
60 s, in place of 600 s, and the writing enumerator runs as a -c
program. TEST_TIME_LIMITS moves to the widened bounds, 120 s in place
of 30 s or 60 s at 5 sites and 240 s in place of 60 s at 1, and gains
main's 2 sites of EnumeratorBounds, at 119 s and 120 s, so it holds
21 entries, the least still 4.5 s; the comment above Stage2Harness
states them. 2 planted forms of TimeLimitSinkProbe bind the TIMEOUT
that main's DoctorCheckpointWrites._doctor reads, as it takes no
timeout argument. No run reported below is of commit 25's tree.

Runs, with python3 -I (3.14.4) on a copy of commit 20, whose tree
commit 21 keeps, with the change of commit 22 applied, on a Linux host
with 96 CPUs whose load was not read, the 3 whole-file runs below
running at the same time:
- tools/test-orch-stage2-hooks.py ran once, 158 tests: it passed, and
  TimeLimitTeardownProbe passed alone, 1 test;
- against copies of the changed file that each change 1 thing, with
  the new test run alone: without the table check in tearDownModule,
  it failed 2 of its 3 subtests of a full run, the 2 with a mismatch;
  with tearDownModule taking every run as full, it failed 3 of its 4
  subtests of a run that is not full, the 3 with a mismatch, and
  tearDownModule failed on 19 entries; each of those 2 runs exited 1;
